title: Transformer
notes: **Transformer:** An electrical device based on mutual induction that changes the voltage level of an AC supply.
It works on the principle of electromagnetic induction: a varying current in the primary coil induces an EMF in the secondary coil via a common magnetic core.
Transformers can be step-up (increase voltage) or step-down (decrease voltage).
confusion: ❌ Assuming transformer works on DC ✅ Transformer only operates on AC as it requires a *changing* magnetic flux to induce EMF (DC has constant flux).

❌ Thinking voltage ratio is independent of current ratio ✅ According to the law of conservation of energy (P_in = P_out for an ideal transformer), voltage and current are inversely proportional: V_p/V_s = I_s/I_p.
❌ Forgetting eddy currents exist in the core ✅ Eddy currents are circular induced currents in the core that cause energy loss as heat; they are minimized by using laminated iron cores.

summary: A transformer changes AC voltage based on mutual induction. It uses the turns ratio to step voltage up or down, while ideally conserving power. Energy losses are mitigated through core design and winding techniques.
specialNotes: Note 1: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. If N_s > N_p, it is a step-up transformer.
Note 2: Transformers operate only on AC.
Note 3: Eddy current loss is reduced by lamination.
Note 4: Hysteresis loss is reduced by using soft iron cores.
Note 5: Efficiency is always less than 100% in practical transformers.
importantStatements: Statement 1: Transformers operate on the principle of mutual induction.
Statement 2: A step-up transformer increases voltage and decreases current.
Statement 3: Flux leakage is a major cause of energy loss.
Statement 4: Frequency of AC remains unchanged in a transformer.
Statement 5: Laminated cores reduce eddy current losses.
importantNotes: Note 1: Power output is always less than power input in practical cases.
Note 2: Use transformer ratio for turns, voltage, and current relationships.
Note 3: DC causes a transformer to burn out due to lack of back EMF/reactance.
Note 4: Study the construction of laminated cores.
Note 5: Flux linkage is assumed to be perfect in an ideal transformer.
examShortTricks: Trick 2: Step-up: N_s > N_p, V_s > V_p, I_s < I_p.
Trick 3: Step-down: N_s < N_p, V_s < V_p, I_s > I_p.
